tagline.en: From a Harvard dorm room to billions of users, now betting the company on AI
tagline.zh: 从哈佛宿舍到数十亿用户，如今把公司押在 AI 上

label.zh: Facebook 上市前股权 + 早期积蓄

label.en: Wealth outside Meta (cash from share sales, real estate, other holdings; estimate)
label.zh: Meta 以外的财富（售股所得现金、房产及其他资产，估算）

t.en: Teenage programmer
t.zh: 少年程序员

desc.en: Grows up in suburban New York, writes software as a schoolboy, then goes to Exeter and Harvard
desc.zh: 在纽约郊区长大，中学时就写软件，之后进入埃克塞特和哈佛

t.en: Dorm-room startup
t.zh: 宿舍里的创业

desc.en: Launches Facebook at Harvard, moves to Palo Alto, raises venture money and refuses to sell
desc.zh: 在哈佛上线 Facebook，搬到帕洛阿尔托，拿到风险投资，拒绝出售公司

t.en: Public and mobile
t.zh: 上市与移动转型

desc.en: A rough IPO, a fast turn to mobile ads, and the Instagram, WhatsApp and Oculus deals
desc.zh: 磕磕绊绊的 IPO，迅速转向移动广告，接连收购 Instagram、WhatsApp 和 Oculus

t.en: Crisis of trust
t.zh: 信任危机

desc.en: Cambridge Analytica, Congress, a record fine and years of scrutiny over privacy and content
desc.zh: 剑桥分析、国会听证、创纪录罚单，以及围绕隐私和内容的多年审视

t.en: Metaverse bet
t.zh: 押注元宇宙

desc.en: Renames the company Meta; the stock loses three quarters of its value in a year
desc.zh: 公司改名 Meta；股价一年内跌去四分之三

t.en: Year of Efficiency
t.zh: 效率之年

desc.en: Cuts costs, restarts growth, launches Threads and sees the stock recover to record highs
desc.zh: 削减成本、重启增长、推出 Threads，股价回升并创下新高

t.en: Superintelligence push
t.zh: 冲刺超级智能

desc.en: Spends more than $100 billion a year on AI while courts hand down verdicts on old harms
desc.zh: 每年在 AI 上投入超过 1000 亿美元，同时法院为过去的伤害接连作出裁决

t.en: Born in White Plains, New York
t.zh: 出生于纽约州白原市

summary.en: Mark Zuckerberg was born in White Plains, New York, and grew up in the nearby suburb of Dobbs Ferry, where he started programming as a schoolboy.
summary.zh: 马克·扎克伯格出生在纽约州白原市，在附近的郊区小镇多布斯费里长大，上中学前就开始写程序。

why.en: Starting point, not scored. Human capital begins at the average level for a child born in the United States.
why.zh: 起点事件，不计分。人力资本以美国同龄人的平均水平作为初始值。

t.en: Graduates from Phillips Exeter Academy
t.zh: 从菲利普斯埃克塞特学院毕业

summary.en: He finished high school at Phillips Exeter Academy, an elite boarding school in New Hampshire. While there he co-wrote Synapse, a music player that learned a listener's taste, which drew interest from large software companies.
summary.zh: 他在新罕布什尔州的名校菲利普斯埃克塞特学院读完高中。在校期间，他与同学合写了能学习听歌习惯的音乐播放器 Synapse，引起了大型软件公司的兴趣。

why.en: An education step: the human-capital target rises as he leaves a top school with a working product to his name. Only the year is known, so the date is year precision.
why.zh: 学历台阶：带着一款真实可用的作品从名校毕业，人力资本目标值上调。只能确认年份，因此日期精度为“年”。

t.en: Enrolls at Harvard College
t.zh: 进入哈佛大学本科

summary.en: He started at Harvard in the autumn of 2002, studying computer science and psychology, and quickly became known on campus for building small web tools for fellow students.
summary.zh: 2002 年秋天他进入哈佛，学习计算机科学和心理学，很快因为给同学做各种小网站工具而在校园里出名。

why.en: Another education step. He left before graduating, so the model treats Harvard as a network and a launch pad rather than a finished degree.
why.zh: 又一级学历台阶。他后来没有读完，所以模型把哈佛看作人脉和起跳板，而不是一张完整的文凭。

t.en: Facemash goes viral and is shut down within days
t.zh: Facemash 走红，几天内被关停

summary.en: He built Facemash, a site that asked students to rate classmates' photos taken from Harvard's online house directories without permission. It spread across campus over a weekend, was taken down, and he was called before the university's Administrative Board.
summary.zh: 他做了一个叫 Facemash 的网站，未经许可从哈佛各宿舍的在线名册里抓取照片，让同学两两比较打分。网站一个周末传遍校园后被关停，他本人被学校纪律委员会传唤。

why.en: Tiny in money terms, but it is the first privacy controversy of his career, so the reputation coefficient takes a small 1% hit. It also showed him how fast a campus network could spread.
why.zh: 金额上可以忽略，但这是他职业生涯里第一场隐私争议，口碑系数小幅 -1%。这件事也让他看到校园社交网络的传播速度。

t.en: Launches thefacebook.com from his Harvard dorm room
t.zh: 在哈佛宿舍上线 thefacebook.com

summary.en: He put thefacebook.com online for Harvard students. Hundreds signed up within days, and the site spread to other universities over the following months. That summer he moved to Palo Alto and did not return to Harvard.
summary.zh: 他把 thefacebook.com 推向哈佛学生，几天内就有数百人注册，随后几个月扩展到其他大学。当年夏天他搬到帕洛阿尔托，此后没有再回哈佛上课。

why.en: The turning point of his life: from this day he owns founder equity. Financial capital switches from pocket money to an estimated stake value, and human capital starts climbing toward the level of a startup founder.
why.zh: 人生转折点：从这一天起他持有创始人股权。金融资本从零花钱切换为估算的股权价值，人力资本开始向“创业公司创始人”的水平爬升。

fin.en: Founder equity enters the model (valued by interpolating between funding rounds).
fin.zh: 创始人股权进入模型（私有阶段按各轮融资估值插值）。

src.name: The Harvard Crimson · Hundreds register for new Facebook website (2004-02-09)

t.en: Peter Thiel makes the first outside investment: $500,000
t.zh: 彼得·蒂尔投入第一笔外部资金：50 万美元

summary.en: PayPal co-founder Peter Thiel put about $500,000 into the young company for roughly 10% of it and joined the board. It was the first outside money and put a price of about $5 million on the business.
summary.zh: PayPal 联合创始人彼得·蒂尔向这家新公司投入约 50 万美元，换取大约 10% 的股份，并加入董事会。这是公司第一笔外部资金，对应估值约 500 万美元。

why.en: First priced round. The stake anchor is an estimate: a valuation near $5 million times an ownership share of roughly half. Sources date the deal to the summer of 2004; the month is approximate.
why.zh: 第一轮有定价的融资。持股价值为估算：约 500 万美元估值乘以大约一半的持股比例。各方资料只说是 2004 年夏天，月份为近似值。

fin.zh: 估算持股价值：约 250 万美元。

t.en: Accel invests $12.7 million at a valuation near $100 million
t.zh: Accel 投资 1270 万美元，估值接近 1 亿美元

summary.en: Venture firm Accel led a $12.7 million Series A that valued the one-year-old company at about $98 million. Later that year the company dropped "the" from its name and became simply Facebook.
summary.zh: 风险投资机构 Accel 领投 1270 万美元的 A 轮融资，这家成立仅一年的公司估值约 9800 万美元。同年晚些时候，公司把名字里的“the”去掉，正式叫 Facebook。

why.en: The stake anchor steps up to roughly $30 million (estimate: valuation times an ownership share of about 30%). Accounts differ on whether the round closed in April or May 2005.
why.zh: 持股价值锚点上调到约 3000 万美元（估算：估值乘以约 30% 的持股比例）。这轮融资完成于 2005 年 4 月还是 5 月，各方说法不一。

fin.zh: 估算持股价值：约 3000 万美元。

t.en: Turns down a sale to Yahoo for about $1 billion
t.zh: 拒绝以约 10 亿美元卖给雅虎

summary.en: Yahoo held serious talks to buy Facebook, with the price reported to reach about $1 billion. Zuckerberg, then 22, chose to stay independent even though several investors and executives favored selling.
summary.zh: 雅虎与 Facebook 认真谈过收购，据报道价格一度谈到约 10 亿美元。当时 22 岁的扎克伯格坚持独立发展，尽管一些投资人和高管倾向于卖掉。

why.en: No money changed hands, so financial capital does not move. The decision later became the standard story about founder conviction, which is why the reputation coefficient gets +2%.
why.zh: 没有任何资金易手，金融资本不变。但这个决定后来成了“创始人定力”的经典故事，因此口碑系数 +2%。

t.en: Facebook opens to anyone aged 13 or older
t.zh: Facebook 向所有 13 岁以上用户开放

summary.en: Facebook dropped the requirement of a school or company email address and let anyone aged 13 or over sign up. The same month it introduced News Feed, which angered many users at first and then became the core of the product.
summary.zh: Facebook 取消了必须使用学校或公司邮箱的限制，13 岁以上的任何人都可以注册。同月推出的动态消息（News Feed）起初引发大量用户抗议，后来成为产品的核心。

why.en: The step from a college site to a mass-market product. The value shows up in later funding rounds; the reputation coefficient gets +2% for the product call that proved right.
why.zh: 从校园网站走向大众产品的一步。价值体现在之后的融资估值里；这个后来被证明正确的产品决定带来口碑系数 +2%。

t.en: Microsoft buys 1.6% of Facebook, valuing it at $15 billion
t.zh: 微软买入 Facebook 1.6% 股份，估值 150 亿美元

summary.en: Microsoft paid $240 million for a 1.6% stake and an advertising partnership, beating Google to the deal. The implied $15 billion price made the 23-year-old founder a billionaire on paper.
summary.zh: 微软出资 2.4 亿美元买下 1.6% 的股份，并拿到广告合作，在竞争中击败了谷歌。150 亿美元的隐含估值让这位 23 岁的创始人成了账面上的亿万富翁。

why.en: The stake anchor jumps to about $4 billion (estimate). Many observers thought the price was inflated by the ad deal, and the next round in 2009 valued the company lower, which the model shows as a dip.
why.zh: 持股价值锚点跳升到约 40 亿美元（估算）。很多观察者认为这个价格被广告合作抬高了，2009 年的下一轮融资估值更低，模型里表现为一段回落。

fin.en: Estimated stake: about $4 billion at the headline valuation.
fin.zh: 按名义估值估算的持股价值：约 40 亿美元。

src.name: Meta Newsroom · Facebook and Microsoft expand strategic alliance

t.en: The film "The Social Network" opens in U.S. cinemas
t.zh: 电影《社交网络》在美国上映

summary.en: David Fincher's film told a dramatized version of Facebook's founding and the lawsuits around it. It was a critical and commercial success and fixed an unflattering picture of Zuckerberg in the public mind, which he said was inaccurate.
summary.zh: 大卫·芬奇执导的这部电影以戏剧化的方式讲述了 Facebook 的创立和相关诉讼。影片叫好又叫座，也把一个并不讨喜的扎克伯格形象刻进了公众印象，他本人表示影片与事实不符。

why.en: Mixed: his fame and audience rose sharply, but the portrait was negative. The model raises the media baseline and applies a small -1% to the reputation coefficient.
why.zh: 影响好坏参半：知名度和受众大幅上升，但人物形象偏负面。模型上调媒体热度基线，同时口碑系数小幅 -1%。

t.en: Named TIME's Person of the Year
t.zh: 当选《时代》周刊年度人物

summary.en: TIME chose the 26-year-old as its Person of the Year for connecting more than half a billion people. In the same month he signed the Giving Pledge, a promise to give away most of his wealth.
summary.zh: 《时代》周刊把 26 岁的他选为年度人物，理由是他把五亿多人连接在了一起。同月他签署了“捐赠誓言”，承诺捐出大部分财富。

why.en: A pure reputation event that no valuation captures, so the reputation coefficient gets +3%.
why.zh: 纯声誉事件，任何估值都反映不了，因此口碑系数 +3%。

src.name: Wikipedia · Time Person of the Year

t.en: Agrees to buy Instagram for about $1 billion
t.zh: 宣布以约 10 亿美元收购 Instagram

summary.en: Weeks before the IPO, Facebook agreed to pay about $1 billion in cash and stock for Instagram, a photo app with 13 employees and no revenue. Zuckerberg negotiated the deal largely by himself.
summary.zh: 上市前几周，Facebook 同意用约 10 亿美元的现金和股票收购 Instagram——一家只有 13 名员工、没有收入的图片应用。这笔交易主要由扎克伯格本人谈成。

why.en: Widely mocked as overpriced at the time and later seen as one of the best acquisitions in technology. The long-run value sits in the share price; the reputation coefficient gets +3% for the judgment.
why.zh: 当时普遍被嘲笑买贵了，后来被视为科技史上最成功的收购之一。长期价值已体现在股价里；这份判断力带来口碑系数 +3%。

src.name: Meta Newsroom · Facebook to acquire Instagram

t.en: Facebook lists on Nasdaq at $38 a share, valued at $104 billion
t.zh: Facebook 以每股 38 美元在纳斯达克上市，估值 1040 亿美元

summary.en: Facebook raised about $16 billion in what was then the largest technology IPO. Trading opened late because of exchange glitches and the stock closed almost exactly at the offer price. Zuckerberg sold about 30 million shares, mainly to cover taxes, and kept voting control.
summary.zh: Facebook 募资约 160 亿美元，是当时规模最大的科技股 IPO。因交易所系统故障，开盘推迟，首日收盘价几乎与发行价持平。扎克伯格卖出约 3000 万股，主要用于缴税，同时保住了投票控制权。

why.en: Anchor switch: from this day financial capital = ownership × shares outstanding × the daily close. His remaining stake of roughly 500 million shares was worth about $19 billion at the offer price (ownership figures are estimates from the prospectus).
why.zh: 锚点切换：从这一天起，金融资本 = 持股比例 × 总股本 × 当日收盘价。他剩下的约 5 亿股按发行价计算约值 190 亿美元（持股数字为根据招股书的估算）。

fin.en: Priced daily from the META (then FB) quote from here on.
fin.zh: 此后按 META（当时代码 FB）日线逐日计价。

src.name: Wikipedia · Initial public offering of Facebook

t.en: Shares close at $17.73, less than half the IPO price
t.zh: 股价收于 17.73 美元，不到发行价的一半

summary.en: In the months after the listing, investors doubted that Facebook could make money on mobile phones, where it showed almost no ads. The stock hit its lowest close on this day. Zuckerberg said he would not sell any shares for at least a year.
summary.zh: 上市后的几个月里，投资者怀疑 Facebook 能否在手机上赚钱——当时它在移动端几乎没有广告。股价在这一天创下收盘最低点。扎克伯格表示至少一年内不会出售任何股票。

why.en: The loss itself is in the share price. The reputation coefficient takes an extra -2% for the botched IPO and the open questions about whether a young founder could run a public company.
why.zh: 损失本身已体现在股价里。IPO 的糟糕表现以及“年轻创始人能否管好上市公司”的质疑，另扣口碑系数 2%。

src.name: Wikipedia · Initial public offering of Facebook

t.en: Mobile reaches 41% of ad revenue; shares jump almost 30% the next day
t.zh: 移动端占广告收入 41%，次日股价大涨近三成

summary.en: Second-quarter results showed that mobile ads, which barely existed a year earlier, already made up 41% of advertising revenue. The stock rose 29.6% on July 25 and soon climbed back above the IPO price.
summary.zh: 二季度财报显示，一年前几乎不存在的移动广告已经占到广告收入的 41%。7 月 25 日股价上涨 29.6%，不久后重新站上发行价。

why.en: The price jump is carried by the stock. The +3% on the reputation coefficient is for proving he could turn the whole company around a new platform in about a year.
why.zh: 股价的跳升由股票自身反映。口碑系数 +3% 是因为他证明了自己能在一年左右把整个公司转向新平台。

t.en: Agrees to buy WhatsApp for about $19 billion
t.zh: 宣布以约 190 亿美元收购 WhatsApp

summary.en: Facebook announced it would pay about $19 billion in cash and stock for the messaging app WhatsApp, which then had around 450 million users and a staff of about 55. It remains the company's largest acquisition.
summary.zh: Facebook 宣布以约 190 亿美元的现金和股票收购即时通讯应用 WhatsApp，当时它有约 4.5 亿用户、约 55 名员工。这至今仍是公司最大的一笔收购。

why.en: The share issue diluted his ownership a little, which the ownership anchors reflect. The reputation coefficient gets +2% for locking up global messaging.
why.zh: 为收购增发的股票略微稀释了他的持股比例，持股锚点已反映这一点。拿下全球即时通讯入口，口碑系数 +2%。

src.name: Meta Newsroom · Facebook to acquire WhatsApp

t.en: Agrees to buy virtual-reality startup Oculus for about $2 billion
t.zh: 宣布以约 20 亿美元收购虚拟现实公司 Oculus

summary.en: Facebook agreed to buy Oculus VR, a headset maker that had not yet shipped a consumer product, for about $2 billion. Zuckerberg called virtual reality the next major computing platform.
summary.zh: Facebook 同意以约 20 亿美元收购当时还没有推出消费级产品的头显厂商 Oculus VR。扎克伯格称虚拟现实是下一个主要的计算平台。

why.en: Scored as mixed: it is the seed of the later Reality Labs division, which went on to lose tens of billions of dollars, and also of the smart-glasses business. A small +1% for long-range ambition.
why.zh: 记为好坏参半：这是后来 Reality Labs 部门的起点，该部门此后累计亏损数百亿美元，但智能眼镜业务也由此而来。长线野心小幅 +1%。

src.name: Meta Newsroom · Facebook to acquire Oculus

t.en: Pledges 99% of his Facebook shares to the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative
t.zh: 承诺把 99% 的 Facebook 股份投入陈-扎克伯格倡议

summary.en: He announced that 99% of his Facebook shares, worth about $45 billion at the time, would go to philanthropic causes over his lifetime through a new organization, the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative. Critics pointed out that it was set up as a company rather than a charity, which keeps control in his hands.
summary.zh: 他宣布，在有生之年把自己 99% 的 Facebook 股份（当时约值 450 亿美元）通过新成立的“陈-扎克伯格倡议”用于公益。批评者指出，该机构是有限责任公司而非慈善基金会，控制权仍在他手里。

why.en: A pledge, not a transfer: the shares stay in his stake until they are actually sold or given, so financial capital does not drop. The reputation coefficient gets +4%.
why.zh: 这是承诺而非过户：股份在真正卖出或捐出之前仍算在他名下，所以金融资本不下降。口碑系数 +4%。

t.en: The Cambridge Analytica data scandal breaks
t.zh: 剑桥分析数据丑闻爆发

summary.en: Newspapers reported that the political consultancy Cambridge Analytica had obtained personal data from tens of millions of Facebook profiles through a quiz app, without users' consent. The stock fell about 7% on the next trading day and Zuckerberg stayed silent for several days before apologizing.
summary.zh: 媒体报道，政治咨询公司剑桥分析通过一款测验应用，在用户不知情的情况下获取了数千万 Facebook 用户的个人数据。下一个交易日股价下跌约 7%，扎克伯格沉默数日后才公开道歉。

why.en: The price drop is in the stock. The lasting damage was to trust in him personally, which the market cannot fully see, so the reputation coefficient takes the maximum -6%.
why.zh: 股价下跌已由股票反映。更持久的伤害是公众对他个人的信任，这是市场看不全的，因此口碑系数扣到上限 -6%。

t.en: Testifies before the U.S. Senate and House over two days
t.zh: 连续两天在美国参众两院作证

summary.en: He answered questions from dozens of senators on April 10 and from a House committee the next day, about ten hours in total, on privacy, election interference and regulation. He took responsibility for the data failures. The stock rose 4.5% on the first day.
summary.zh: 4 月 10 日他接受数十名参议员质询，次日又出席众议院委员会听证，两天合计约十小时，话题涉及隐私、选举干预和监管。他表示对数据问题负责。作证首日股价上涨 4.5%。

why.en: Mixed: being summoned at all confirmed how serious the crisis was, but his composed performance calmed investors. The price reaction is in the stock; a small +1% offsets part of the earlier hit.
why.zh: 好坏参半：被传唤本身说明危机之重，但他沉稳的表现安抚了投资者。股价反应已在股票里；口碑系数小幅 +1%，抵消此前的一部分扣分。

src.name: U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee · Hearing record (2018-04-10)

t.en: Shares fall 19% in a day, erasing about $119 billion
t.zh: 股价单日下跌 19%，市值蒸发约 1190 亿美元

summary.en: After second-quarter results, the company warned that revenue growth would slow and that spending on safety and privacy would squeeze profit margins. The stock fell 19%, at the time the largest one-day loss of market value for any U.S. company.
summary.zh: 二季度财报发布后，公司警告收入增速将放缓，安全和隐私方面的投入会压低利润率。股价下跌 19%，创下当时美国上市公司单日市值损失的最高纪录。

why.en: Fully priced by the market, so no extra reputation shock (rep = 0). His stake lost roughly $16 billion that day.
why.zh: 完全由市场定价，不再额外扣口碑（rep = 0）。他的持股当天缩水约 160 亿美元。
